transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came because something in me feels… turned off, I suppose. Even when my children come and sit with me, and they’re trying to be kind, or when the sun is out on my garden—which used to make me feel peaceful, you know, just seeing the light on the plants—I don’t feel it. I know I should feel glad, or comforted, or at least a little warmed by it, but inside I’m just flat.

It’s like the part of me that could take in anything good has shut down. I can see that these are good things happening around me, but I can’t seem to feel them. That’s why I’m here.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About two weeks now. It started right after my husband collapsed… in our kitchen. The paramedics came and worked on him right there, on the floor, and ever since that day I just haven’t felt like myself. I keep thinking maybe it’s only been a few days, but no—it’s been about two weeks of feeling this strange flatness, like something in me hasn’t come back on since then.
Are you still able to enjoy activities that you normally found pleasurable before your husband's collapse?

No… not really. I mean, I can still do some of the things, I suppose. I can sit by the window, I can look out at my garden, I can have my children come over and sit with me, talk to me, bring me tea or fuss over whether I’ve eaten. And I know, in my head, those are the things that used to give me comfort. My garden especially—seeing the sun on the leaves, the little bits of color, that used to settle me.

But now it’s like it doesn’t reach me. I look at it and I know it’s beautiful, but I don’t feel pleased. My children are there, and I know I love them, I know I should feel comforted by them being near me, but inside I just feel flat. Almost like there’s a pane of glass between me and anything good. The part of me that could feel glad or warmed by those things feels as if it just shut off.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

I… I don’t know if sad is the right word. That’s what I keep trying to sort out, actually. People expect me to say I’m sad, and maybe I am in some way, but most of the time it doesn’t feel like crying sadness. It’s more like there’s nothing there, or not enough of anything there.

I’ll sit there and think, “Shouldn’t I be feeling something?” And I know what happened was awful, and I know what I’ve lost, but when you ask if I feel sad most of the time, I can’t honestly say it feels that clear. It’s not like a wave of sadness all day long. It’s more flat… blank, I suppose. Sometimes I think I’m sad underneath it, but I can’t quite reach it.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in since your husband's collapse?

No… I can’t really say there are. I keep trying to find one, because it seems like there should be something. My children come and sit with me, and they’re kind, they really are. They talk to me, they try to make the house feel normal. And I sit there knowing I ought to feel comforted by them, but it just doesn’t land inside me the way it used to.

Even my garden… the sun can be on it just right, and I can see that it’s pretty. I know it’s pretty. But I don’t feel that little lift I used to feel. That’s really why I came, I think—because even when the things that should bring me peace are right in front of me, I feel flat inside, like the part of me that could be glad or soothed has just shut off.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since your husband's collapse?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve lost a significant amount, no—not that anyone has told me, and I haven’t been weighing myself carefully. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything like that.

I suppose I haven’t been paying very close attention to it. The days sort of go by, and I eat what’s put in front of me, or I don’t notice much either way. But as far as actual weight loss, I couldn’t give you a number. I haven’t noticed anything major.
Do you often feel guilty since your husband's collapse?

Guilty… I don’t know. I’ve turned that word over in my head a few times, because people say things like, “Don’t blame yourself,” and I’m not even sure that’s exactly what I’m doing.

I wouldn’t say I feel guilty most of the time, no. At least not in a clear way. It’s more that my mind goes back over things and I wonder about little moments—what I noticed, what I didn’t notice, whether I should have understood something sooner. But then I also don’t know if that’s guilt or just… trying to make sense of something that doesn’t make sense.

So I suppose the honest answer is I’m not sure. I don’t sit there thinking, “This was my fault,” not exactly. It’s more muddled than that.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live since your husband's collapse?

I… I don’t quite know how to answer that. Not in a neat yes-or-no way.

I don’t think I’ve sat there and made any kind of plan, if that’s what you mean. I haven’t… I haven’t thought it through like that. But there are moments when everything feels so heavy and so unreal that I think, “How am I meant to keep going like this?” And then I feel frightened even hearing myself think that, because I don’t know whether that counts as not wanting to live or just being exhausted by all of it.

It’s more that I don’t recognize my life right now. I wake up and there’s this feeling of, “Oh, it’s still true,” and I almost don’t know what I’m supposed to do with another whole day. But I’m not sure I would call that wanting to die. I don’t know. I’m sorry, I know that’s not very clear. I just… I’m not sure.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

I’m not sure. I haven’t really been watching myself from the outside, if that makes sense. I don’t know whether I’m actually moving more slowly, or whether everything just feels slower to me because I’m… well, because I’m not quite myself.

Speaking, I don’t know either. Sometimes I feel like it takes me longer to find what I’m trying to say, and then I go round in circles a bit, but I don’t know if someone else would say I’m speaking more slowly. No one has pointed it out to me.

With moving, I suppose I’m not rushing about the way I used to, but I’m 81, so I’m never exactly darting around the house anyway. I haven’t noticed anything very clear like dragging my feet or people telling me to hurry up. I just can’t say for certain.
Do you feel like you're having trouble getting out of bed in the morning due to feeling heavy or sluggish?

I don’t know that I’d say “heavy” exactly. I mean, mornings are difficult, but I’m not sure if it’s because my body feels sluggish in that way or because I lie there trying to gather myself before I move.

Some mornings I do stay in bed longer than I probably should, but I’m not always thinking, “I physically can’t get up.” It’s more confused than that. I wake up and there’s this sort of pause where I have to remember what day it is and what I’m supposed to be doing, and then I think about getting up, and I don’t do it straight away.

But I haven’t really noticed my limbs feeling like lead, if that’s what you mean. I’m old, so getting up is never exactly graceful anymore, but I can’t tell whether it’s different in that particular heavy, sluggish way. I suppose I’d say I’m not sure.
Do you feel like your movements have become slower than they used to be?

I’m not really sure. I know you asked something close to that before, and I’m trying to think about it properly, but it’s hard for me to separate what’s actually slower from what just feels slower inside my head.

I don’t have a clear sense that I’m moving in slow motion or anything like that. No one has said, “You’re walking slowly,” or “Why are you taking so long?” At least not that I can remember. I do find myself sort of stopping before I do things, like I’ll stand there for a moment and think, “What was I doing?” but I don’t know if that means my movements are slower, or if I’m just hesitating more.

I suppose I’m not as quick and purposeful as I normally like to be around the house, but at my age it’s difficult to judge. Some days I’ve always been slower than others. So… I can’t honestly say yes. I haven’t noticed a definite change like that.
Have you noticed any change in how your clothes fit since your husband's collapse?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really been paying close attention to that sort of thing. I mean, I get dressed, but I’m not standing in front of the mirror checking whether things are looser or tighter, if you see what I mean.

Some clothes always fit a bit differently depending on the day anyway, especially at my age—waistbands, blouses, all of that. I haven’t noticed anything clear like needing a different size, or something hanging off me, or not being able to button things. No one has mentioned anything to me either.

So I don’t think I can say there’s been a definite change in how my clothes fit since it happened. If there has been, I haven’t really noticed it.
Do you often feel worthless since your husband's collapse?

I don’t know if I’d call it worthless. That’s a strong word, isn’t it? I’ve never really thought of myself in those terms, even now. I do feel… shaken, and not like myself, and there are moments when I sit there and think I’m not handling things the way I should be, but I’m not sure that’s the same as feeling worthless.

I suppose I do question myself more than I used to. Like, I’ll think, “Why can’t I keep myself together better?” or “Why am I just sitting here?” But I don’t walk around thinking I have no value or that I’m useless as a person. It’s more that everything feels difficult to get a grip on, and I’m not always sure what I’m supposed to be doing with myself.

So… often? No, I don’t think so. Not worthless exactly. More unsettled and unsure of myself, if that makes sense.
Have you lost a noticeable amount of weight since your husband's collapse, such as having to tighten your belt or feeling like your clothes are looser than they used to be?

I really don’t know. I haven’t noticed anything like that in a definite way. I’m not using a belt much, so I can’t say I’ve had to tighten one, and with my clothes… well, some things are loose anyway and some things never fit the same from one wash to the next.

I haven’t looked at myself and thought, “Oh, I’ve lost weight,” and no one has said anything to me about it. I don’t weigh myself regularly either, so I wouldn’t want to pretend I know. Since it happened, I’ve mostly just been getting dressed and getting through the day, not really checking how things fit.

So no, not a noticeable amount that I can say. If there has been any change, it hasn’t been clear enough for me to notice.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to end your life since your husband's collapse?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that properly. I don’t think I’ve had thoughts like a plan, or sitting there deciding to do something to myself, if that’s what you mean.

There have been moments where I’ve felt so overwhelmed that I think, “I can’t bear this,” or “I don’t know how I’m supposed to go on with things feeling this way,” but that isn’t the same as wanting to end my life, at least not to me. It’s more like everything feels too much in that moment, and I want it to stop feeling so awful.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve wanted to end my life. Not in a real, deliberate way. I’ve just felt frightened and worn down by it all.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless, or having trouble sitting still?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m pacing the floor all day or anything like that. I do catch myself adjusting in the chair sometimes, or wringing my hands a bit, but I don’t know if that’s more than anyone would do when they’re upset or just sitting too long.

Trouble sitting still… maybe at times, but it’s hard for me to judge. Sometimes I sit and sit and hardly move, and other times I feel like I can’t quite get comfortable, like I’m shifting around without really meaning to. But I haven’t especially thought, “Oh, I’m restless,” if that makes sense.

So I suppose my answer is… I don’t know that I’ve noticed it clearly. Maybe a little here and there, but not something I can describe very confidently.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless more often than you used to?

More often than I used to… I honestly don’t know. I mean, I’m older, so I have always shifted around a bit if I sit too long, and sometimes my hands just do what they do, you know, smoothing my sleeve or picking at a tissue. I can’t say I’ve been keeping track of whether it’s more than before.

Since all this happened, I’m probably more aware of every little thing my body does, if that makes sense. I notice myself sitting there and then I think, “Am I moving too much? Am I not?” But before, I never paid attention to that sort of thing, so it’s hard to compare.

I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. Maybe there have been times when I felt unsettled and moved around more, but whether it’s actually more often than I used to… I can’t really say.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight since your husband's collapse?

I don’t really know. I haven’t weighed myself properly, not in a way where I could tell you a percentage like that. Five percent… I’m not even sure what that would be for me without doing the arithmetic.

My clothes maybe feel a little different some days, but then I don’t know if that’s real or just how I’m noticing everything more. I haven’t been standing on the scale and keeping track, so I’d be guessing, and I don’t want to say yes or no too firmly when I honestly don’t know.

So… I haven’t noticed a clear weight loss like that, but I can’t give you a definite number.
Do you feel like you have been speaking more slowly than usual since your husband's collapse?

Speaking more slowly… I’m not sure. I haven’t really been listening to myself that way. I know sometimes I pause because I’m trying to find the right words or I lose my train of thought for a moment, but whether my actual speaking is slower than it used to be, I don’t know.

No one has said to me, “You’re talking slowly,” at least not that I can recall. And when I’m upset or tired I suppose anyone might take longer to get a sentence out, but I can’t say I’ve noticed a definite change.

So I’d say… I’m not sure. Maybe I hesitate more at times, but I don’t know if I’m speaking more slowly overall.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or agitated most of the time?

Most of the time… I don’t know that I can say that exactly. I do get unsettled sometimes, like I can’t quite get comfortable in my own chair, and I may move my hands around or get up and start doing some little thing and then not really know why I stood up. But “most of the time” sounds very big, and I’m not sure I could honestly measure it that way.

Some moments I’m just sitting quietly, and I might look calm from the outside, I suppose. Other times I feel sort of keyed up, but I don’t always know if that’s agitation or just being tired or having too much on my mind. I’m not very good at separating those things out.

So… I’d say I have noticed periods of restlessness, yes, but whether I’m restless or agitated most of the time, I’m not sure. I wouldn’t want to overstate it.
